report:
**Conclusion:** Yes. Systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials consistently show that offering HIV self-testing (HIVST) alongside standard testing services significantly increases overall HIV testing uptake.

**Key Supporting Evidence:**
* **Higher Testing Rates:** Meta-analyses of randomized trials demonstrate that adding HIVST roughly doubles testing completion rates compared to standard facility-based services alone.
* **Reaching Priority Populations:** HIVST successfully reaches first-time testers and groups with historically lower clinic attendance—including men, key populations, and sexual partners—by addressing barriers such as stigma, inconvenience, and privacy concerns.
* **Policy Guidance:** Based on robust global evidence, the World Health Organization endorses HIVST as an effective strategy to expand testing coverage.

**Nuances and Limitations:**
* **Linkage to Care:** While initial test completion rises, facilitating clinical confirmatory testing and linkage to treatment (ART) for individuals who test positive can be more challenging without direct healthcare provider supervision.
* **Comprehensive STI Screening:** Offering HIVST increases HIV test uptake specifically, but it may not automatically improve screening rates for other sexually transmitted infections.

**Sources:**
* https://researchonline.lshtm.ac.uk/id/eprint/4661682/
* https://journals.plos.org/plosmedicine/article?id=10.1371/journal.pmed.1004270
* https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44203-024-00003-6
* https://researchonline.lshtm.ac.uk/id/eprint/4676009/1/Tumushime-etal-2025-Do-community-level-factors-play-a-role.pdf
